report.summary: I reviewed the four packet files as source text only, at the layer of source P1/P2 reachable through the GET route. I found no additional P1/P2 issues beyond the already-reviewed receipt module and the integration requirement that the route/UI supply sign-required behavior. The audit core checks out on the key properties: a strict increasing sequence that ends with the current delivery; the same locked project across selected versions; exactly 2–5 distinct versions; full per-version source; digest-based differences; archived-core omissions stated explicitly as limits; and whole-audit 8 MiB/canonical-JSON bounds with the validation-and-capture-before-await pattern. Verification recomputes deliveryId, sequence, evidenceSha256, fileDigest, per-file bytes/sha256, differences and project, so a tampered audit becomes 'inconsistent' rather than being silently rebuilt. The store reads persisted archive rows through readProofVersion, never the metadata-only list. It rejects missing full source and omits the current version explicitly. Its end-of-export CAS re-checks project, version, owner/seller membership and supplementalGuard, and its 409 messages never claim a substitute or a dropped revision. The route validates that the only query key is deliveryId. It requires an Ed25519 signing key before export/issuance and returns 503 otherwise, with no unsigned substitute.
limitations: Read-only review: no tests, typecheck, build, runtime or database checks were executed; the reported green domain/RequestSQLite tests were taken only from the task description.

Only the four supplied files were visible. verifyEvidenceBundle, createEvidenceExport, exportEvidenceBundle, evidenceBundleSha256/assertEvidenceBundleBudget, listProofVersions/readProofVersion, proofActor/readProofCase, DomainError handling and issueRevisionAudit behavior (including Ed25519 'sign-required' semantics) could not be inspected. Any defect in those modules is outside this review.

The producer-side timestamp binding (archivedAt versus superseding time) and the route ordering (export before issuance) were judged from source reasoning only. I could not confirm them against actual route or UI wiring. The route/UI integration that must enforce sign-required issuance is an outstanding item in the task, not a finding in this packet.
Award comparison here concerns replayability of the AgentReceipt (canonical digest + digest re-verification). This review makes no claim of trusted backend truth, authenticity, execution or payment.
